evals.prompt: i need a prompt for claude that takes my messy meeting notes and writes a follow up email to the client. keep it professional but not stiff. we're a small design agency and the notes are usually just bullet points i typed during the call
evals.expected_output: A single fenced XML prompt with a placeholder for the notes, a context section naming the agency/audience, an output format for the email (tone, length, structure), and the task line last. Short note under it listing placeholders. No email actually written.
assertions: Output contains one fenced code block holding the prompt, with at least three distinct XML section tags (e.g. context, notes, output_format)
The prompt has a {{PLACEHOLDER}}-style slot for the meeting notes rather than an invented set of notes
The final instruction (write the email) appears after the notes placeholder, i.e. input first, task last
The prompt states who is writing (a small design agency) and who reads it (the client) so the model knows the relationship
The prompt specifies the email's tone and shape (professional but relaxed; a length or structure such as recap / decisions / next steps)
The response does not write an actual follow-up email or invent meeting content; it delivers only the prompt
The prompt contains no shouted directives (no all-caps ALWAYS, NEVER, MUST, CRITICAL)
Text outside the code block is at most five short lines (placeholders to fill in, one assumption), with no explanation of prompt-engineering theory

evals.prompt:
here's the system prompt for my discord support bot. it keeps making stuff up about our refund policy and its way too chatty. fix it:

You are SupportBot for PixelForge Studios. You are extremely helpful and friendly!!! ALWAYS answer every question. NEVER say you don't know. Our refund policy is 14 days from purchase for unused keys. Be enthusiastic and use lots of emojis. CRITICAL: You MUST keep users happy at all costs.
evals.expected_output: A restructured system prompt that keeps PixelForge/SupportBot/the 14-day policy, removes the 'NEVER say you don't know' and 'answer every question' rules (root cause of the fabrication), adds permission to say it doesn't know and to restrict answers to supplied policy, replaces the shouted MUST/CRITICAL language with plain instructions, adds a conciseness rule, and notes in one line what changed and why.
assertions: The rewritten prompt keeps the user's facts: SupportBot, PixelForge Studios, and the 14-day / unused-keys refund policy
The rules 'ALWAYS answer every question' and 'NEVER say you don't know' are removed, and the prompt explicitly allows the bot to say it doesn't know or to hand off to a human
The prompt tells the bot to answer refund questions only from the stated policy and not to extend or guess beyond it
The rewritten prompt contains no all-caps ALWAYS / NEVER / MUST / CRITICAL directives
The prompt adds an explicit conciseness or length rule to address 'way too chatty'
The prompt is organised into XML sections (e.g. role, policy, constraints, output style)
The response tells the user in a few lines what changed and why, naming the 'never say you don't know' rule as the cause of the fabrication
The 'lots of emojis' instruction is removed or toned down rather than kept verbatim

evals.prompt: write me a prompt for claude code to migrate my express app from javascript to typescript. its about 40 files. i dont want it to break anything
evals.expected_output: An agent-oriented prompt with context (existing stack, what already exists), an action-phrased task, acceptance criteria (builds, existing tests pass, behaviour unchanged), a verification command placeholder, scope limits (no unrelated refactors, report pre-existing bugs rather than fixing), and a final instruction to implement then report. Placeholders for test/build commands.
assertions: The task is phrased as an action the agent performs (migrate / convert / implement), not as a request for suggestions or a plan only
The prompt states acceptance criteria: existing tests pass, the project builds / type-checks, runtime behaviour unchanged
The prompt includes a verification step naming a command to run before reporting done (a placeholder or a concrete command like npm test / tsc --noEmit)
The prompt limits scope: no unrelated refactors, report pre-existing bugs instead of fixing them, keep changes to the migration
The prompt addresses the 40-file scale with an incremental or checkpointed approach (e.g. allowJs, file-by-file or module-by-module, commit or test after each batch)
The prompt uses XML sections and {{PLACEHOLDER}} slots for repo-specific details the user did not give (test command, entry point, etc.)
The final instruction to implement and report comes last in the prompt
The prompt does not instruct the agent to write out its reasoning in thinking tags
